## Endpoint

**`POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/with-timestamps`**, with `Content-Type: application/json`.

Regional servers: `https://api.us.elevenlabs.io`, `https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io`, `https://api.in.residency.elevenlabs.io`, `https://api.sg.residency.elevenlabs.io`.

## Path parameter

- `voice_id` (string, required): the voice to use. The doc points to `GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices` to list voices.

## Query parameters

- `enable_logging` (boolean, default `true`): `false` enables zero retention mode, which makes history features unavailable, including request stitching. Enterprise customers only.
- `optimize_streaming_latency` (integer, nullable, **deprecated**): 0 to 4. Higher values trade quality for latency. 4 turns off the text normalizer and can mispronounce numbers and dates. Default is none.
- `output_format` (enum, default `mp3_44100_128`): codec, sample rate, and bitrate, e.g. `mp3_22050_32`. Allowed values include `mp3_*`, `opus_*`, `pcm_*`, `wav_*`, `alaw_8000`, and `ulaw_8000`. MP3 at 192 kbps requires Creator tier or above. PCM and WAV at 44.1 kHz require Pro tier or above.

## Request body

- `text` (string, **required**): text to convert to speech.
- `model_id` (string, default `eleven_multilingual_v2`): the model must support text to speech. The doc says to check the `can_do_text_to_speech` property from `GET /v1/models`.
- `language_code` (string, nullable): ISO 639-1 code to enforce a language for the model and text normalization. Ignored if the model doesn't support it. **Not supported for `multilingual_v2` models.**
- `voice_settings` (object, nullable): overrides the stored voice settings for this request only (see below).
- `pronunciation_dictionary_locators` (array): applied in order. Up to 3 locators, each with `pronunciation_dictionary_id` (required) and `version_id` (nullable; latest is used if omitted).
- `seed` (integer, nullable): 0 to 4294967295. Best-effort determinism. Same seed and parameters should return the same result, but this isn't guaranteed.
- `previous_text` (string, nullable): text preceding this request, for continuity. Ignored if `previous_request_ids` is also sent.
- `next_text` (string, nullable): text following this request, for continuity. Ignored if `next_request_ids` is also sent.
- `previous_request_ids` (array of string): up to 3 request IDs of earlier samples. Best results when the same model is used.
- `next_request_ids` (array of string): up to 3 request IDs of following samples. Useful for regenerating a clip while keeping flow with its neighbors. Best results when the same model is used.
- `use_pvc_as_ivc` (boolean, nullable): use the IVC version of a professional voice. The doc says this may improve expressiveness and reduce latency.
- `apply_text_normalization` (enum, default `auto`): `auto`, `on`, or `off`. `auto` lets the system decide (e.g., spelling out numbers).
- `audio_effects` (object, nullable): see below.
- `apply_language_text_normalization` (boolean, default `false`, **deprecated**): **Japanese only**. The doc warns it can greatly increase latency.

### `voice_settings` fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stability` | double, nullable | 0.5 | Not stated. Lower values give broader emotional range. Higher values can sound monotonous. |
| `use_speaker_boost` | boolean, nullable | true | n/a. Boosts similarity to the original speaker at a small latency cost. |
| `similarity_boost` | double, nullable | 0.75 | Not stated. Controls how closely output adheres to the original voice. |
| `style` | double, nullable | 0 | Not stated. Amplifies the original speaker's style and may add latency if not 0. |
| `speed` | double, nullable | 1 | Not stated. Below 1.0 slows speech; above 1.0 speeds it up. |
| `clone_strength` | double, nullable | none | 0 to 1. Applies only to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the v4 model. The doc recommends 0 for most cases and 0.5 as a fallback. |

### `audio_effects` fields (EffectsSpec)

- `filter_preset_id` (string, nullable): a voice-coloring preset such as `phone` or `old_radio`.
- `distance` (double, default 0): 0 (close) to 1 (far).
- `environment_id` (string, nullable): reverb environment such as `small_room` or `hall`. Reverb is stereo and adds a tail of several seconds.
- `background_noise_id` (string, nullable): looped background bed such as `cafe` or `keyboard`.
- `send_level` (double, default 1): 0 to 1. Reverb feed level. Only applies when `environment_id` is set.
- `pan` (double, default 0): -1 to 1. Pans only the voice.

Reverb or a non-zero `pan` is rejected with 400 for `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, and `pcm_*` formats. Unknown IDs return 404. Effects don't change request cost.

## Response (200)

- `audio_base64` (string, **required**): base64-encoded audio.
- `alignment` (object, nullable): character timing for the original text.
- `normalized_alignment` (object, nullable): character timing for the normalized text.

Both alignment objects contain these required fields:
- `characters` (array of string)
- `character_start_times_seconds` (array of double)
- `character_end_times_seconds` (array of double)

## Errors

- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: validation error with `detail`, an array of objects containing `loc` (string or integer array), `msg` (string), and `type` (string).

## Model-specific notes

The doc states these limits:
- `language_code` is not supported for `multilingual_v2`.
- `clone_strength` applies only to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the v4 model.
- `apply_language_text_normalization` is supported only for Japanese.
- `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated, and its best achievable latency varies by model.

- `next_request_ids` (array of string): up to 3 request IDs of following samples. Useful for regenerating a clip while keeping flow with its neighbors. Best results when the same model is used.
- `use_pvc_as_ivc` (boolean, nullable): use the IVC version of a professional voice. The doc says this may improve expressiveness and reduce latency.
- `apply_text_normalization` (enum, default `auto`): `auto`, `on`, or `off`. `auto` lets the system decide (e.g., spelling out numbers).
- `audio_effects` (object, nullable): see below.
- `apply_language_text_normalization` (boolean, default `false`, **deprecated**): **Japanese only**. The doc warns it can greatly increase latency.

### `voice_settings` fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stability` | double, nullable | 0.5 | Not stated. Lower values give broader emotional range. Higher values can sound monotonous. |
| `use_speaker_boost` | boolean, nullable | true | n/a. Boosts similarity to the original speaker at a small latency cost. |
| `similarity_boost` | double, nullable | 0.75 | Not stated. Controls how closely output adheres to the original voice. |
| `style` | double, nullable | 0 | Not stated. Amplifies the original speaker's style and may add latency if not 0. |
| `speed` | double, nullable | 1 | Not stated. Below 1.0 slows speech; above 1.0 speeds it up. |
| `clone_strength` | double, nullable | none | 0 to 1. Applies only to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the v4 model. The doc recommends 0 for most cases and 0.5 as a fallback. |

### `audio_effects` fields (EffectsSpec)

- `filter_preset_id` (string, nullable): a voice-coloring preset such as `phone` or `old_radio`.
- `distance` (double, default 0): 0 (close) to 1 (far).
- `environment_id` (string, nullable): reverb environment such as `small_room` or `hall`. Reverb is stereo and adds a tail of several seconds.
- `background_noise_id` (string, nullable): looped background bed such as `cafe` or `keyboard`.
- `send_level` (double, default 1): 0 to 1. Reverb feed level. Only applies when `environment_id` is set.
- `pan` (double, default 0): -1 to 1. Pans only the voice.

Reverb or a non-zero `pan` is rejected with 400 for `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, and `pcm_*` formats. Unknown IDs return 404. Effects don't change request cost.

## Response (200)

- `audio_base64` (string, **required**): base64-encoded audio.
- `alignment` (object, nullable): character timing for the original text.
- `normalized_alignment` (object, nullable): character timing for the normalized text.

Both alignment objects contain these required fields:
- `characters` (array of string)
- `character_start_times_seconds` (array of double)
- `character_end_times_seconds` (array of double)

## Errors

- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: validation error with `detail`, an array of objects containing `loc` (string or integer array), `msg` (string), and `type` (string).

## Model-specific notes

The doc states these limits:
- `language_code` is not supported for `multilingual_v2`.
- `clone_strength` applies only to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the v4 model.
- `apply_language_text_normalization` is supported only for Japanese.
- `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated, and its best achievable latency varies by model.

The Voice Library's notice period gives users advance warning when a voice owner stops sharing a voice they've saved or used.

- **Without a notice period**, a voice is removed immediately, and anyone who saved it loses access right away.
- **Length:** Notice periods range from 30 days to 2 years. Owners earn higher rewards for longer periods.
- **During the notice period**, the voice leaves the Voice Library, but users who previously saved or used it keep access. They receive email and in-app notifications.
- **Deletion during the notice period** prevents re-saving, since the voice is no longer in the library.
- **Checking the end date:** The app shows when a voice will be disabled. API users can find this in the `disable_at_unix` field of the Get Voice endpoint response. The field is `null` or absent if no notice period is active.
- **Webhooks:** Account owners can set up webhook notifications for voice removal, which helps when you need to notify customers immediately.

The Voice Library's notice period gives users advance warning when a voice owner stops sharing a voice they've saved or used.

- **Without a notice period**, a voice is removed immediately, and anyone who saved it loses access right away.
- **Length:** Notice periods range from 30 days to 2 years. Owners earn higher rewards for longer periods.
- **During the notice period**, the voice leaves the Voice Library, but users who previously saved or used it keep access. They receive email and in-app notifications.
- **Deletion during the notice period** prevents re-saving, since the voice is no longer in the library.
- **Checking the end date:** The app shows when a voice will be disabled. API users can find this in the `disable_at_unix` field of the Get Voice endpoint response. The field is `null` or absent if no notice period is active.
- **Webhooks:** Account owners can set up webhook notifications for voice removal, which helps when you need to notify customers immediately.

The main answer is in ElevenLabs' request stitching docs. The guide says the feature is not available for the eleven_v3 model. Its example code uses a different model, `eleven_v4`, so that model may be the one to use instead.

Other points from the results:
- **Request limit:** The guide says the API accepts at most 3 previous request IDs, and requests with more return a 400 error. Its example passes the most recent IDs with the newest last.
- **Completion requirement:** A previous request must have finished processing before its request ID can be used for conditioning. For streaming, that means the audio must be fully read from the response body.
- **Zero retention conflict:** Setting `enable_logging` to false turns on zero retention mode, which disables history features, including request stitching, for that request (When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. This will mean history features are unavailable for this request, including request stitching.).
- **previous_text vs. previous_request_ids:** In case both previous_text and previous_request_ids is send, previous_text will be ignored.
- **Dialogue endpoints:** The text-to-dialogue docs describe `previous_text` as limited to 100 characters and not supported by every model. Their request ID fields carry the same "not supported by every model" caveat.

Values below 1.0 will slow the voice down, to a minimum of 0.7. Values above 1.0 will speed up the voice, to a maximum of 1.2. Speed is not available for the Eleven v3 model. **Stability, similarity, and style ranges:** Not covered. The page only says that "Voice settings like Stability and Similarity help control the consistency" (about 75 characters), while emotion comes from the text.

**Seed and determinism:** Output is nondeterministic. "The models are nondeterministic. For consistency, use the optional seed parameter" (about 80 characters). Subtle differences may still occur.

**Timestamps:** Not covered.

**Request stitching:** To keep prosody natural across chunks, use the "previous_text / next_text parameters" (about 45 characters). The page also mentions previous and next request IDs.

**Voice types and plan availability:** The page lists voice library, professional and instant cloning, and voice design. It does not describe default voices. On plans, "The voice library is not available via the API to free tier users." (about 70 characters)

**Consistency advice:** Use the seed parameter for more consistent output. For large text, split it into segments and stream.

**Character-per-credit cost:** No base per-character rate is given. The page only says Flash v2.5 offers a "50% lower price per character for API generations" (about 65 characters).

# ElevenLabs facts for the Shorts production guide (checked 2026-11-13)

Most items are confirmed from official elevenlabs.io pages, but `help.elevenlabs.io` returned HTTP 403 on every attempt. I read the same articles through the official mirror at `elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/...` instead. Quotes come through WebFetch's page reader, which sometimes declined to return full text, so re-check any quote before publishing it as verbatim.

Two findings change the guide:
- **Default voices are being retired:** they expire on December 31, 2026 (see item 6).
- **There is a newer model:** Eleven v4 (`eleven_v4`, `eleven_v4_turbo`) now exists, and Turbo v2/v2.5 are listed as deprecated.

## 1. Plans and prices
URL: https://elevenlabs.io/pricing

| Plan | Monthly price | Credits/month | Commercial license |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 10k | Not listed |
| Starter | $6 ("Then $6 per month", $1 first month) | 30k | Yes ("Commercial License") |
| Creator | $22 ($11 first month) | 121k | Yes |
| Pro | $99 | 600k | Yes |
| Scale | $299 | 1.8M (3 seats) | Yes |
| Business | $990 | 6M (10 seats) | Yes |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Yes |

- **Annual billing:** the FAQ says "two months free".
- **Cancelling:** "your account will be downgraded to the Free plan and any unused paid credits will expire."
- **Free plan attribution:** not stated on the pricing page. It is confirmed at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/legal/can-i-publish-the-content-i-generate-on-the-platform.md : "must attribute it to ElevenLabs by including "elevenlabs.io" or "11.ai" in the title".
- **Rollover:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/billing says "Up to two months' worth of unused credits can roll over to the next month."
- **Sizing (my arithmetic, not from a page):** 30 videos x 2,500 characters = 75,000 characters a month. At 1 credit per character that exceeds Starter (30k) and fits Creator (121k).

## 2. Credits per character per model
- **All listed models, website:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/technical/what-models-do-you-offer-and-what-is-the-difference-between-them.md gives 1 credit per character, excluding credit multipliers, for Eleven v4, Multilingual v2, Flash v2.5, Flash v2, Turbo v2.5 and Turbo v2. This is the reader's summary, not a direct quote.
- **Eleven v3:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/core-capabilities/text-to-speech/how-much-does-it-cost-to-generate-using-eleven-v3-alpha.md : "The cost of generating with Eleven v3 is 1 credit per character on the website." and "API generations are discounted - see API pricing for details."
- **General rule:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/account/general/have-characters-changed.md : "each text 'character' you generate into speech will consume 1 credit". It adds: "some shared voices in our Voice Library have a custom rate that applies a multiplier to your credit consumption."
- **Pricing page:** https://elevenlabs.io/pricing says "1 text character equals 1 credit" for V2 Multilingual, and Flash/Turbo cost "between 0.5 and 1 credit per character" for API usage.
- **API pricing:** https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api says "API usage is billed in US dollars, not credits." The price per 1K characters is "$0.08" for v4, v3 and v2 Multilingual, and "$0.04" for Flash / Turbo and v4 Turbo.
- **Model list:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/models gives per-request limits of 10,000 characters for `eleven_v4`, 5,000 for `eleven_v3`, 40,000 for `eleven_flash_v2_5` and 10,000 for `eleven_multilingual_v2`. It lists `eleven_turbo_v2_5` and `eleven_turbo_v2` as deprecated.

## 3. Commercial use
- **Paid plans:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/legal/can-i-publish-the-content-i-generate-on-the-platform.md : "All paid plans include a commercial license, provided you're not using Beta Services."
- **Free plan:** same page: "The free plan does not include a commercial license and cannot be used for any commercial purpose."
- **Before or after a subscription:** same page: "Content created outside of a paid subscription (before or after) cannot be used commercially".
- **After cancelling:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/account/general/what-happens-to-my-content-after-my-subscription-ends says you "will still have a commercial license" for content generated during the subscription. The reader returned only that fragment; the search snippet of the help.elevenlabs.io version adds "forever".
- **Terms:** https://elevenlabs.io/terms-of-use §1(c)(i) for free users: "you may only use the Services for non-commercial purposes". §1(c)(ii) for paid users: "you may use the Services for commercial purposes". §4(c)(ii): "you retain all rights in and to your Output."
- **Billing doc:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/billing : "When generating content on our paid plans, you get commercial rights to use that content." and "If you are on the free plan, you can use the content non-commercially with attribution."
- **YouTube:** no official page names YouTube monetization as permitted; it follows from the commercial license.

## 4. Timestamps endpoint
URL: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert-with-timestamps

- **Path:** `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/with-timestamps`
- **Response fields:** `audio_base64` (string), `alignment` and `normalized_alignment` (both nullable).
- **Alignment contents:** each has `characters`, `character_start_times_seconds` and `character_end_times_seconds`. Timing is character-level only, so word timings must be derived from the characters.
- **Defaults:** `model_id` defaults to `eleven_multilingual_v2`; `output_format` defaults to `mp3_44100_128`.
- **Model support:** NOT VERIFIED. The page lists no per-model restriction for this endpoint.

## 5. voice_settings, seed and stitching
- **Defaults** (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert-with-timestamps and https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/voices/settings/get): `stability` 0.5, `similarity_boost` 0.75, `style` 0, `use_speaker_boost` true, `speed` 1.
- **Numeric ranges:** the API reference states no min or max for `stability`, `similarity_boost` or `style`. The 0 to 1 range is from my memory, NOT VERIFIED.
- **Speed range:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/playground/text-to-speech : "Values below 1.0 will slow the voice down, to a minimum of 0.7." and "Values above 1.0 will speed up the voice, to a maximum of 1.2." This is the product guide, not the API reference.
- **Model limits on settings:** the same guide says speed, similarity and speaker boost are unavailable for Eleven v3. https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/core-capabilities/text-to-speech/what-is-eleven-v4.md : "Style and Speed sliders are not available in Eleven v4, and SSML is not supported."
- **Recommended values:** "The most common setting is stability around 50, similarity around 75, and keeping style at 0," and "we recommend keeping this setting at 0 at all times" (style).
- **`seed`:** integer from 0 to 4294967295, best-effort determinism and not guaranteed (API reference, paraphrased). https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/text-to-speech : "The models are nondeterministic. For consistency, use the optional seed parameter".
- **`previous_text` / `next_text`:** ignored when `previous_request_ids` / `next_request_ids` are also sent (API reference, paraphrased).
- **`previous_request_ids`:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/text-to-speech/request-stitching : "You can provide at most 3 request IDs in `previous_request_ids`." and "The request IDs should be no older than two hours." and "Request stitching is not available for the `eleven_v3` model."

## 6. Keeping one voice consistent
- **Non-determinism:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/playground/text-to-speech : "setting the sliders to specific values won't guarantee the same results every time." So fix the `voice_id`, `model_id`, settings and `seed`, and expect small variation anyway.
- **v4 drift:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/text-to-speech/eleven-v4 : "Eleven v4 is under active, continuous development." and "its behavior may shift over time as quality improves". Multilingual v2 is the more stable choice for 30 matching videos a month (my inference).
- **My Voices:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/voices/voice-library : "Voices saved from the Voice Library do not use custom voice slots."
- **Notice period:** same page: "The minimum notice period is 30 days, and the maximum is 2 years." With one, "you'll receive advance notice through email and in-app notifications." Without one, "you'll lose access to the voice immediately." If you delete the voice during the notice period, "it cannot be saved again."
- **Checking the end date:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/voice-customization/voice-library/what-is-a-notice-period says the `disable_at_unix` field of the Get Voice endpoint gives it (paraphrased). The Voice Library can be filtered by notice period.
- **Already generated audio:** https://elevenlabs.io/vla : "any Outputs generated using your User Voice Model prior to the end of the Notice Period will continue to exist". ElevenLabs can also remove voices itself: "we reserve the right to review and remove any User Voice Model made available in the Voice Library".
- **Default voices retired:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/voices/my-voices/what-are-default-voices.md : "All our Default voices will expire on December 31, 2026, and they will no longer be accessible after this date." Also: "Default voices are only available for accounts that were created before March 2026." Replacements are not identical: "this is not a strict 1-to-1 replacement, and tone and style may differ." The page maps each old voice to a new one, for example Brian `nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb` to Sawyer `8dEUmyPMdDdK91vboYih`.

## 7. Voice Library policy and YouTube
- **Commercial license:** https://elevenlabs.io/elevenlabs-voices-a-comprehensive-guide : "All voices in the Voice Library come with a free commercial use license." This is a marketing guide, not the terms; the publish article in item 3 still requires a paid plan.
- **Restriction:** https://elevenlabs.io/voice-library/commercial : "Yes, you can use the commercial voices in your commercial project." and "we ask that you do not sell or license our tools or use the output to develop competitive products or services."
- **Free users:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/voices/voice-library : "Some voices in the Voice Library are only available to users with a paid subscription." and "Voice Library voices are not available via the API to free tier users."
- **Credit multipliers:** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/voices/voice-library/why-cant-i-use-some-voices-from-the-voice-library.md : "When you use a voice with a credit multiplier, the credit usage will be adjusted accordingly."
- **YouTube monetization article:** NOT VERIFIED as described. The help-center index has no article on monetizing YouTube with AI voices. The only YouTube-related one is https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/legal/audio-detector/will-watermarks-cause-my-content-to-be-flagged-downranked-or-demonetized-on-you-tube-or-other-platforms.md : "No other platforms can currently detect ElevenLabs watermarks." and the watermark "is not connected to other platforms' monetization or content policies".
- **Blog:** https://elevenlabs.io/blog/how-to-make-money-using-ai-in-youtube appeared in search but I did not open it.

## 8. Voice types by plan
- **Default voices:** only for accounts created before March 2026, and they expire December 31, 2026 (item 6). Replacements are in the Voice Library.
- **Voice Library:** usable on Free in the app except restricted voices; not available through the API on Free (item 7).
- **Voice Design:** listed under the Free plan on https://elevenlabs.io/pricing . https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/billing : "The free plan offers three custom voice slots". Only Professional Voice Clones can be shared to the library.
- **Instant Voice Clone:** https://elevenlabs.io/pricing lists "Instant Voice Cloning" starting at Starter. The billing doc agrees: "Cloning is only available on the Starter tier and above."
- **Professional Voice Clone:** listed from Creator on the pricing page. Scale shows "3 Professional Voice Clones" and Business "10 Professional Voice Clones".

## NOT VERIFIED
1. Anything directly on `help.elevenlabs.io` (HTTP 403). I used the elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center mirrors.
2. The exact sentence on keeping the license after cancelling. I have only the fragment "will still have a commercial license"; "forever" is from a search snippet.
3. Which models support `/with-timestamps`. From memory only: it works with Multilingual v2 and Flash v2.5; v3 and v4 are unknown.
4. Min and max for `stability`, `similarity_boost` and `style` in the API (0 to 1 is from memory).
5. Whether the API enforces the 0.7 to 1.2 speed range (it comes from the product guide).
6. Whether `seed`, `previous_text` and `next_text` work on `eleven_v4`. Only the v3 stitching exclusion is confirmed.
7. Credits charged against a subscription for API calls. The pricing page says 0.5 to 1 credit per character for Flash/Turbo; the API pricing page says the API is billed in dollars. Budget 1 credit per character.
8. A dedicated ElevenLabs article on YouTube monetization: none found in the help-center index.
9. Whether a signup page offering Instant Voice Cloning on Free is current. It appeared only in a search snippet and conflicts with the pricing page and billing doc.
10. A per-plan count of voice slots; the pricing comparison table came through garbled.
11. A terms clause explicitly granting commercial use of Voice Library voices. The VLA does not use the phrase; the only sources are the marketing pages in item 7.
